newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Incitec says plant shut-down to cost A$10m.
newsitem.headline: Incitec says plant shut-down to cost A$10m.

text.p: Chemicals and fertiliser group Incitec Ltd said it expected the temporary shutdown of its Brisbane nitrogen manufacturing plant for an upgrade would cost the company about A$10 million.
Incitec managing director Jim Babon also said expectations the company would build a new fertiliser plant in Victoria mainly stemmed from media speculation.
"We have made no progress on that front," he told Reuters.
Babon said earlier the one-and-a-half months shutdown of the Brisbane plant for scheduled maintenance and a major ammonia plant upgrade would have a significant impact on second half profits.
"International fertiliser prices are also softening - the trend is downwards," Babon said.
"However we are not expecting the full-year result to be a disaster," he said.
Babon said the Brisbane plant upgrade would result in the plant becoming more world-competitive.
Incitec is about 70 percent owned by ICI Australia Ltd .
